commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. commands.name: update-config

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Based on my search of the Mistral documentation, **I cannot find specific version compatibility information** between transformers 4.57.3 and mistral-common 1.8.5 in the available docs.

The documentation mentions installing `mistral-common` for tokenizer integration ([migration guide](https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/migration-guides#migrate-from-llama)), but doesn't provide a version compatibility matrix for transformers.

To resolve this, I recommend checking:

1. **transformers package metadata** — Check what mistral-common version transformers 4.57.3 requires:
   ```bash
   pip index versions transformers==4.57.3
   # or check: https://pypi.org/project/transformers/4.57.3/
   ```

2. **mistral-common releases** — Check the PyPI page for mistral-common:
   ```bash
   pip index versions mistral-common
   # or check: https://pypi.org/project/mistral-common/
   ```

3. **Try upgrading both** — Update to the latest compatible versions:
   ```bash
   pip install --upgrade transformers mistral-common
   ```

The error suggests there's an API mismatch, likely because transformers 4.57.3 expects a different mistral-common API than version 1.8.5 provides. Checking PyPI's dependency graphs should show which versions are tested together.
